rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes cold rolling and aging to introduce dislocations and precipitates, whereas the hidden target uses molecular-dynamics simulations varying individual element concentrations (Nb, Ta, Ti, Zr) in a defect-minimized crystal. These are fundamentally different kinds of interventions.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies cold rolling, aging at 600–800 °C, and testing elastic moduli up to 1100 K and creep at 1250 °C. rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes dislocation networks and precipitate-induced thermal expansion mismatch. These are different classes of mechanism.

The hidden target predicts nonmonotonic strength/modulus changes with composition and temperature-dependent degradation, with no creep or hardness measurements. The predicted properties and directions are unrelated.
